paper_title: PyramidInfer Pyramid KV Cache Compression for High-throughput LLM   Inference
caption: The perplexity standard deviations when only PvCs are reserved at each layer.
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the perplexity standard deviation (log) across different layers when only Pyramid Vectors (PvCs) are reserved at each layer, as described in the context of the PyramidInfer method for high-throughput LLM inference. The x-axis, labeled "Layer," represents the layer index in the model, ranging from 0 to approximately 35, with tick marks at intervals of 10. The y-axis, labeled "Perplexity (log) Std," measures the standard deviation of perplexity on a logarithmic scale, ranging from 0.00 to 1.75, with major gridlines and tick marks at intervals of 0.25. The data is represented by a single line in a light orange color, marked with small circular points. The line begins at a high value of approximately 1.75 at layer 0, exhibiting a sharp decline to around 0.25 by layer 2. It then gradually decreases further, leveling off to a value near 0.00 for layers beyond approximately 15, remaining at or near zero for the remaining layers.
